THIS CRL.P IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 CR.P.C BY THE ADVOCATE FOR THE PETITIONER PRAYING THAT THIS HON'BLE COURT MAY BE PLEASED TO QUASH THE ABOVE CASE PENDING AGAINST THE PETITIONERS BEARING NO.C.C.NO.18517/2019 PENDING BEFORE CHIEF METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE AT BENGALURU FILED BY 2nd RESPONDENT UNDER SECTION 498-A, 354 READ WITH SECTION 3 AND 4 OF DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT READ WITH 34 OF IPC.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

This petition is filed by the husband and his family members challenging the initiation of criminal proceedings against them for the offences punishable under Section 498A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioners files a memo enclosing a copy of the order sheet of the Family Court in respect of M.C.No.5038/2019 which was a proceeding initiated for divorce by the husband.
He relies upon the NC: 2024:KHC:20833 order sheet dated 04.04.2024 to indicate that the parties have settled their disputes amicably and the wife had agreed to receive a sum of Rs.25 lakhs.

It is also submitted that under the terms of the said settlement, it has been jointly agreed that the wife would agree to co- operate in closing/quashing the proceedings in C.C.No.18517/2019 and as a consequence, the petitioner would withdraw Criminal Petition No.6392/2019 i.e, the present petition.
3.

In view of the fact that the husband and wife have settled their disputes amicably as indicated in the order sheet of the Family Court and also the fact that the marriage has stood dissolved on the basis of the joint memo filed, no useful purpose would be served by continuing the proceedings.

It is also noticed that as indicated in the terms of the settlement, a sum of Rs.25 lakhs has been paid to the wife and hence, it is a fit case which requires to be closed in order to ensure that the parties adhere to the terms of the settlement.
NC: 2024:KHC:20833
Consequently, the proceedings initiated against the petitioners shall stand quashed.
4. The petition is accordingly disposed off.
